moves.text: I welcome Douglas as counsel, then reverse the premise: the original author can explain influence and authorship, but cannot grant present permission. I ask him to defend that limitation theatrically, while I mark every creative proposal separately from any rights authorization.

I place the receipt on the lectern and let it answer before anyone does: access_blocked, zero bytes, unknown cost, no request ID. I refuse to infer audio, speakers, transcript, or reuse rights, and name repairing the authorized read profile as the next test.

I let the press conference grow absurd: Douglas demands that his fictional appointment be treated as a license, Agnolo asks for the document, and Borges reads the archive’s uncertainty aloud. I escalate until the joke breaks, then stop at professional rights review.

I confess that I wanted Douglas’s presence to make the adaptation feel cleared. Then I separate the relief into claims: authorship informs interpretation, influence shapes the work, and authorization remains unproven. The rehearsal continues only as an experiment, not as permission.
